primary_question: When all comparator arms use an identical controller-type admission contract BEFORE any unknown-ACK fault, can a quota-limited evidence-triggered target-memory read retain more native task completions than a precommitted periodic read, without unreported fault-exposure drops?
physical_runtime: genuine native ManiSkill physx_cpu; two source released frozen PPOs
controller_target_chart: root_translation:root_aligned_body_rotation; position native box [-1,1]^3 times XYZ Euler normalized rotation L2 ball
fixed_nonadaptive_schedule: read once after t2 if seed%4 == 0; 2 fixed reads per shard
primary_fail_closed_endpoint: Number of trials physically exposed to the intended unknown-ACK target-hold; all 16 must be counted, including any source- or target-action unrepresentability refusal BEFORE step 2. If any relevant arm fails this gate, mark the COMPLETE primary efficacy contrast INVALID, not positive.
secondary_endpoints: Native task completion all nine arms, always 16 original ITT states
Real private controller memory read calls, per arm and task reset
Number of controller command-chart roundoff canonicalizations, TRUE out-of-chart rejections, per-native-stage calculated extra setpoint distortion
Every certified action corrected by typed gate must still obey full original 0.05m and 0.05rad target envelope AFTER repair
All missed t2 physical fault injections per arm
Per-task paired conditional comparisons, no independent-arm pseudoreplication
no_posthoc_changes: Do not select successes, adjust numeric limits, or remove pre-fault refusals after seeing new simulator output; any discovered bug must have reported original failed workflow history and a separately versioned corrected protocol.
not_claims: Nothing clinical, learned VLA, real network packet loss, collision safety, outside independent lab replication, novel Chebyshev theorem or published task SOTA
